candidates.title: Activation of the Mercury Laser: A Diode-Pumped Solid-State Laser Driver for Inertial Fusion
candidates.notes: Mercury laser activation paper (LLNL, 2001). States performance goals of 10% electrical efficiency at 10 Hz, 100 J per pulse for IFE DPSSL. Most direct published benchmark for DPSSL WPE targets at IFE-relevant rep rates. Accessible PDF via OSTI purl.

candidates.title: Diode laser pumps for future inertial fusion energy systems
candidates.notes: Optics Express (October 2025). Covers diode pump requirements for 10-20 Hz DPSSL beamlines for IFE. Most recent (2025) authoritative review of pump technology requirements. Documents 70% efficiency for diode bars as enabling metric. Tangentially relevant to WPE (addresses pump component, not end-to-end system efficiency), but provides the IFE community's current view of required efficiencies.

candidates.title: High average power ultrafast laser technologies for driving future advanced accelerators
candidates.notes: Focuses on laser plasma accelerators for particle physics colliders, not DPSSL IFE drivers. No IFE or wall-plug efficiency data.

candidates.title: Status and prospects for inertial fusion energy via lasers (Betti)
candidates.notes: General IFE status review. Does not address DPSSL wall-plug efficiency specifically.

candidates.title: Mercury and Beyond: Diode-Pumped Solid-State Lasers for Inertial Fusion Energy
candidates.notes: Earlier (1999/2000) Mercury design overview. Same 10% WPE goal as 15013216 but pre-activation. Redundant with 15013216 which reports actual system activation.

candidates.title: Prospects for Inertial Fusion Energy Based on a Diode-Pumped Solid-State Laser Driver
candidates.notes: 1997 paper discussing DPSSL IFE feasibility. Older than Mercury program papers; likely contains efficiency targets but not achieved results.

candidates.title: HAPLS — LLNL project page
candidates.notes: HAPLS at ELI-Beamlines: 10 Hz, 1 PW, 30 J. No wall-plug efficiency data published on project page.

gaps_attempted.notes: G-5 remains partial: no source documents achieved wall-plug efficiency for a DPSSL system at IFE-relevant operating conditions. Both extracted sources document the 10% WPE as a design goal or diode-level efficiency metric, not a demonstrated end-to-end result. Mercury laser (15013216) is the best available analogue — it explicitly targets 10% WPE at 10 Hz, 100 J for IFE use, consistent with HB11's claimed target. The 2025 diode pumps paper (3008974) provides the most current view of pump diode efficiency requirements. Marvel Fusion's specific DPSSL WPE remains uncharacterized in public sources — this appears to be a genuine information gap rather than a missed source.
